choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: (A) insulated from (B) intertwined (C) ripple 근거 ❸❹❼❾ 해설: (A) ❸ separate and thereby buffered from the effects of errors = 외부 실수로부터 차단된(insulated from) / (B) ❹ 더 이상 그렇지 않다 + ❼ This interdependence = 깊이 얽힌(intertwined) / (C) ❾ instantly spreads the impact of small failures = 빠르게 파급되다(ripple). exposed to(~에 노출된)는 ❸의 ‘보호되었다’와 반대, isolated(고립된)는 ❹·❼과 반대이고 뒤의 so 결과(실패가 퍼짐)와도 맞지 않음, fade(사라지다)는 ❾의 ‘확 산’과 반대. 요약문 해석: 과거에 기관들은 서로 떨어져 있었고, 그로 인해 다른 곳에서 일어난 실수로부터 (A) 차단되어 있었다. 그러나 오늘날 정보 기술은 시스템들 을 깊이 (B) 얽혀 있게 만들었고, 그래서 한 곳의 사소한 실패가 네트워크 전체로 빠르게 (C) 파급될 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Social media has altered business, politics, and friendships, making going viral a household term. ❷ The global financial industry links every bank and countless households in every country, making us vulnerable to human error taking place on the other side of the world. ❸ As Columbia University strategy professor Rita McGrath explains, years ago most of our institutions were separate and thereby buffered from the effects of errors outside their walls. ❹ That is no longer the case. ❺ The digitization of massive amounts of information has continued to grow enormously as the cost of computing power has decreased. ❻ The development of smart systems that communicate autonomously gave rise to an infinite variety of potential breakdowns. ❼ This interdependence is a breeding ground for complex failure. ❽ As Rita puts it, when “things that used to be kept separate bump up against each other, it becomes far more difficult to predict what’s going to happen next.” ❾ Information technology creates new vulnerabilities because interconnectedness instantly spreads the impact of small failures.
choice.body: In the past, institutions stood apart from one another, which kept them (A)________ mistakes made elsewhere. Today, however, information technology has made systems deeply (B)________, so a minor failure in one place can (C)________ rapidly through the whole network.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: connecting systems makes each of them sturdier and less likely to break down
only poorly designed smart systems are in danger of suffering serious failures
complex failures are mostly caused by careless users rather than by technology
farms that raise animals with new technology often fail to breed healthy livestock
systems that depend heavily on one another create ideal conditions for complicated breakdowns to arise
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 이러한 상호 의존성은 복합적 실패의 온상이다 → 서로 의존하는 시스템들은 복잡한 고장이 생겨나기 좋은 조건을 만든다 해설: ‘온상(breeding ground)’은 무언가가 생겨나고 자라기 좋은 환경의 비유이다. ‘This interdependence’는 ❺❻의 디지털화·자율 소통 시스템이 만 든 상호 의존을 가리키고, 뒤의 ❽(분리되어 있던 것들이 부딪치면 예측이 어려움)·❾(작은 실패가 즉각 확산)가 ‘복합적 실패가 생겨나기 좋은 조건’이라는 의미를 확인해 준다. 가축 번식은 breeding을 문자 그대로 읽은 함정, ‘연결하면 더 튼튼해진다’는 정반대, ‘설계가 형편없는 시스템만’은 원인을 일부로 축 소한 범위 왜곡, ‘부주의한 사용자 탓’은 원인을 기술 밖으로 돌린 무관한 진술. ① 시스템들을 연결하면 각각이 더 튼튼해지고 고장 날 가능성이 줄어든다 ② 설계가 형편없는 스마트 시스템만이 심각한 고장을 겪을 위험이 있다 ③ 복잡한 실패는 기술보다는 주로 부주의한 사용자들에 의해 일어난다 ④ 새로운 기술로 동물을 기르는 농장은 건강한 가축을 번식시키는 데 자주 실패한다 ⑤ 서로에게 크게 의존하는 시스템들은 복잡한 고장이 생겨나기에 이상적인 조건을 만든다
choice.body: The development of smart systems that communicate autonomously gave rise to an infinite variety of potential breakdowns. This interdependence is a breeding ground for complex failure. As Rita puts it, when “things that used to be kept separate bump up against each other, it becomes far more difficult to predict what’s going to happen next.”
choice.ul: a breeding ground for complex failure.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

(A) mild — (B) heightened — (C) ongoing yet survivable
(A) mild — (B) lightened — (C) ongoing yet survivable
(A) lethal — (B) lightened — (C) ongoing yet survivable

choice.ex: (A) mild (B) lightened (C) ongoing yet survivable 근거 ❸❹❺ 해설: (A) ❸ the cowpox virus, which is harmless to humans = 순한(mild) 바이러스 / (B) ❹ contributed enormously to the reduction of the burden = 부담을 덜어 주었다(lightened) / (C) ❺ deadly → chronic manageable = 지속되지만 견뎌 낼 수 있는(ongoing yet survivable). lethal(치 명적인)은 ❸의 ‘인간에게 무해한’과 반대, heightened(높였다)는 ❹의 ‘감소’와 반대, sudden and fatal(급작스럽고 치명적인)은 ‘once-fatal(한때 치명 적이었던)’과 모순. 요약문 해석: 의학은 전염병에 맞서 엄청난 진보를 이루었다. Jenner는 (A) 순한 바이러스와의 접촉이 치명적인 바이러스로부터 사람들을 보호할 수 있다 는 것을 발견했고, 그 이후 실험실에서 만든 백신은 많은 질병의 부담을 크게 (B) 덜어 주었다. 오늘날 치료 덕분에 한때 치명적이었던 일부 바이러스성 질 병은 (C) 지속되지만 견뎌 낼 수 있는 질환이 되었다.
choice.psg: ❶ Scientific developments and technologies in medical practice have brought us enormous progress in the treatment and prevention of infectious diseases. ❷ The discovery of penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming, for which he later received the Nobel Prize, was one of the biggest breakthroughs in the battle against infectious diseases. ❸ Edward Jenner discovered around 1796 that humans were protected against the deadly smallpox virus after exposure to the cowpox virus, which is harmless to humans. ❹ Vaccines developed in laboratories have contributed enormously to the reduction of the burden of bacterial and viral diseases and have even led to the elimination of poxvirus. ❺ For other infectious diseases (for example cholera and malaria), control and hygiene management measures have reduced their burden, while for others treatment therapies turned viral diseases that were deadly into chronic manageable diseases.
choice.body: Medical science has made huge progress against infectious diseases. Jenner found that contact with a (A)________ virus could shield people from a deadly one, and lab-made vaccines have since greatly (B)________ the burden of many diseases. Today, thanks to therapy, some once-fatal viral illnesses have become (C)________ conditions.

(A) spread — (B) avoid — (C) sanitation
choice.ex: (A) cure (B) avoid (C) sanitation 근거 ❶❷❸❹❺ 해설: ❶ treatment and prevention의 두 축: (A) ❷ 페니실린 = 감염을 치료하다(cure) / (B) ❸❹ Jenner의 발견·백신 = 걸리기 전에 질병을 피하다 (avoid, 예방) / (C) ❺ 콜레라·말라리아는 control and hygiene management measures = 위생(sanitation). spread(퍼뜨리다)는 ‘강력한 치료 수 단’과 모순, catch(걸리다)는 ‘보호(예방)’와 반대, medication(약물 치료)은 ❺에서 ‘또 다른 질병(for others)’의 방법이라 콜레라·말라리아와 짝이 맞지 않음. 요약문 해석: 의학은 크게 두 가지 방식으로 전염병에 맞서 진보를 이루었다. 페니실린은 감염을 (A) 치료하는 강력한 방법을 제공했고, Jenner의 발견과 이후의 백신은 사람들이 질병이 덮치기 전에 그것을 (B) 피하도록 도왔다. 콜레라와 말라리아의 경우에는 개선된 (C) 위생이 부담을 낮추기도 했다.

For cholera and malaria, improved (C)________ has also lowered the burden.

choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 전염병과의 싸움 → 사람 사이에 옮는 질병을 물리치려는 의학(인류)의 오랜 노력 해설: ‘전투(battle)’는 실제 전쟁이 아니라 인류(의학)가 전염병을 이겨 내려는 노력의 비유이다. ❶ ‘전염병의 치료와 예방에서의 엄청난 진보’가 그 싸움 의 내용이고, ❸ 천연두 예방, ❹ 백신, ❺ 위생 조치·치료법이 모두 같은 싸움의 사례이다. 감염된 상처로 죽은 병사들의 전쟁은 battle을 문자 그대로 읽은 함정, 노벨상 경쟁은 같은 문장의 Nobel Prize를 이용한 범위 왜곡, 세균의 반격은 싸움의 주체를 뒤집은 것, 신약 안전성 논쟁은 무관. ① 병사들이 감염된 상처로 자주 목숨을 잃었던 전쟁들 ② 노벨상을 받으려는 과학자들 사이의 경쟁 ③ 세균이 약에 내성을 갖게 되면서 반격하는 방식 ④ 새로운 약이 안전한지를 둘러싼 대중적 논쟁 ⑤ 세균과 바이러스가 일으키는 질병을 물리치려는 의학의 오랜 노력
choice.body: Scientific developments and technologies in medical practice have brought us enormous progress in the treatment and prevention of infectious diseases. The discovery of penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming, for which he later received the Nobel Prize, was one of the biggest breakthroughs in the battle against infectious diseases. Edward Jenner discovered around 1796 that humans were protected against the deadly smallpox virus after exposure to the cowpox virus, which is harmless to humans.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.

choice.ex: (A) impartially (B) studying (C) in light of 근거 ❶❷❸❽ 해설: (A) ❶❷ 우리는 사용자가 아니고 만든 것에 너무 가까워 objectively 볼 수 없다 = 공정하게(impartial y) 판단할 수 없다 / (B) ❸ observations of real users = 실제 사람들을 연구(studying) / (C) ❽ based on the findings from representative users = ~에 비추어(in light of). swiftly(신속하게) 는 본문에 근거 없는 판단 기준, instructing(가르치는)은 관찰의 방향을 뒤집은 것, regardless of(~와 상관없이)는 ❽의 based on과 정반대. 요약문 해석: 디자이너는 사용자가 아니기 때문에 자신의 제품을 (A) 공정하게(객관적으로) 판단할 수 없다. 그러므로 가장 좋은 인터페이스는 실제 사람 들이 제품을 사용할 때 그들을 (B) 연구하는 데서 나오며, 사용성 테스트는 디자이너가 대표적인 사용자들이 드러내는 것에 (C) 비추어 작업을 개선할 수 있게 해 준다.
choice.psg: ❶ A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. ❷ We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. ❸ The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. ❹ So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? ❺ An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. ❻ The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. ❼ This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. ❽ Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.
choice.body: Designers cannot judge their own products (A)________, since they are not the users. The best interfaces therefore come from (B)________ real people as they use a product, and usability testing lets designers improve their work (C)________ what representative users reveal.

choice.ex: (A) shortcomings (B) refine (C) typical 근거 ❻❽ 해설: (A) ❻ uncover problems in a design = 디자인의 결점(shortcomings) / (B) ❽ improve their work through subsequent revisions = 여러 차 례 다듬다(refine) / (C) ❽ representative users = 전형적인(typical) 사용자. production costs(생산 비용)는 본문에 없는 내용, abandon(버리다)은 ‘개선’과 반대, expert(전문가)는 대표적인(일반) 사용자와 반대. 요약문 해석: 사용성 테스트는 참가자들에게 실생활과 같은 과제를 수행하게 함으로써 사용자들의 습관과 취향뿐 아니라 디자인의 (A) 결점을 드러낸다. 그러면 디자이너는 (C) 전형적인 사용자들에게서 얻은 결과의 안내를 받아 여러 차례의 변경에 걸쳐 제품을 (B) 다듬을 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. ❷ We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. ❸ The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. ❹ So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? ❺ An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. ❻ The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. ❼ This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. ❽ Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.
choice.body: Usability testing reveals a design’s (A)________ as well as users’ habits and tastes by having participants carry out true-to-life tasks. Designers can then (B)________ their products over several rounds of change, guided by findings from (C)________ users.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Usability testing can reveal opportunities that designers had not noticed.
The results of usability testing can be used to make a design better over time.
Watching how real users interact with an interface helps produce better interfaces.
Usability testing gives designers a sense of how a design will work in real use.
Experienced designers can predict user behavior more accurately than inexperienced ones.
choice.ex: 본문은 디자이너의 경험 정도를 비교하지 않는다. 오히려 ❶❷는 디자이너라면 누구나(we) 사용자가 아니고 자기 작업에 너무 가까워 객관적으로 볼 수 없다고 말하므로, ‘경험이 많으면 더 정확히 예측한다’는 상식적 주장은 추론할 수 없다(본문에 없는 비교, 상식 함정). ① 근거 ❻ — 사용성 테스트는 디자이너가 알아차리지 못했던 가능성을 드러낼 수 있다. ② 근거 ❽ — 사용성 테스트의 결과는 시간이 지나면서 디자인을 더 좋게 만드는 데 사용될 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❸ — 실제 사용자들이 인터페이스와 어떻게 상호 작용하는지 지켜보는 것은 더 나은 인터페이스를 만드는 데 도움이 된다. ④ 근거 ❼ — 사용성 테스트는 디자이너에게 디자인이 실제 사용에서 어떻게 작동할지 감을 준다. ⑤ 근거 없음(정답) — 경험 많은 디자이너는 경험이 적은 디자이너보다 사용자 행동을 더 정확하게 예측할 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. ❷ We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. ❸ The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. ❹ So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? ❺ An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. ❻ The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. ❼ This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. ❽ Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: designers care so much about users that they ignore their own ideas
designers are so familiar with their own creations that they cannot judge them as an outsider would
designers spend too little time on what they build to understand it

choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 우리는 우리가 만드는 것에 너무 가깝다 → 자기 작품에 너무 익숙해서 사용자(외부인)의 눈으로 객관적으로 볼 수 없다 해설: ‘너무 가깝다(too close)’는 물리적 거리가 아니라 자기 작품에 대한 지나친 친숙함·애착의 비유이다. 같은 문장의 to objectively see it(객관적으로 볼 수 없다)과 ❶ we are not the user(우리는 사용자가 아니다)가 의미를 확인해 주고, ❸ 실제 사용자 관찰이 그 해결책이다. 화면에 가까이 앉는다는 문 자 그대로의 해석, 시간을 너무 적게 들인다는 것은 ‘너무 가까움(깊이 관여)’과 반대, 사용자를 너무 신경 쓴다는 것은 문제의 방향을 뒤집은 것, 바빠서 마 감을 못 지킨다는 것은 무관. ① 디자이너는 사용자를 너무 신경 써서 자신의 아이디어를 무시한다 ② 디자이너는 자기 창작물에 너무 익숙해서 그것을 외부인처럼 판단할 수 없다 ③ 디자이너는 자신이 만드는 것에 너무 적은 시간을 들여서 그것을 이해하지 못한다 ④ 디자이너는 물리적으로 화면에 너무 가까이 앉아 있어서 작은 실수를 알아차리지 못한다 ⑤ 디자이너는 너무 바빠서 프로젝트를 제때 끝내지 못한다
choice.body: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them.
choice.ul: We’re much too close to what we build

choice.ex: (A) interpret (B) hopeful (C) pile up 근거 ❶❸❾⓫ 해설: (A) ❶ changing the way one thinks about emotional situations, ❸ it can be construed in different ways = 상황을 어떻게 해석하느냐 / (B) ❽❾ 두 번째 해석은 더 낮은 강도의 슬픔과 함께 희망·강인함·감사 같은 긍정적 감정 = 희망적인 / (C) ❿⓫ 반복되면 단기적 감정 결과들이 축적되어 (accumulate) 심리적 건강을 형성 = 쌓이다. 상황을 ‘피하는’ 것은 본문의 재평가(다르게 생각하기)와 무관하고, ‘적대적인’ 감정은 두 번째 해석이 불러오 는 긍정적 감정과 반대이며, ‘사라지다’는 축적되어 건강을 형성한다는 ⓫과 정반대. 요약문 해석: 우리가 감정적인 상황을 어떻게 (A) 해석하는지가 우리가 느끼는 것을 형성한다. 똑같은 이혼도 강렬한 분노를 불러올 수도, (B) 희망적인 감 정이 섞인 더 약한 고통을 불러올 수도 있다. 그러한 변화가 시간이 지나며 (C) 쌓이면 우리의 정신 건강을 강화할 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Reappraisal — changing the way one thinks about emotional situations — might present a particularly effective avenue to regulating emotions because it transforms emotions at their root. ❷ Take, for example, someone who is going through a divorce. ❸ This is often an adverse event, and yet, it can be construed in different ways. ❹ One might view it as an overpowering loss that will mark one’s family for life. ❺ Alternatively, one might see it as something that is painful but that might lead to positive outcomes in the long run, such as improved relationships. ❻ As a result of these different construals, one might feel different emotions. ❼ The first construal may bring intense sadness and anger. ❽ The second construal might also bring sadness and anger but perhaps at lower levels. ❾ Crucially, it might also bring some positive emotions, such as hope, strength, or gratitude. ❿ This example illustrates how reappraisal might powerfully transform short-term emotional responses. ⓫ When repeated over time, these short-term emotional consequences of reappraisal might accumulate to shape people’s psychological health. ⓬ Thereby, reappraisal might be a key to resilience.
choice.body: How we (A)________ an emotional situation shapes what we feel: the same divorce can bring intense anger or milder pain mixed with (B)________ feelings. When such shifts (C)________ over time, they can strengthen our mental health.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: The second view is more accurate than the first, since divorce usually improves family relationships.

choice.ex: ❺는 두 번째 해석이 이혼을 ‘장기적으로 관계 개선 같은 긍정적 결과로 이어질 수도 있는(might)’ 일로 본다고 했을 뿐이다. 필자는 두 해석 중 어느 쪽이 더 ‘정확한지’ 판단하지 않으며, 두 해석이 서로 다른 감정을 낳는다는 점(❻~❾)만 보여 준다. 또 ❸은 이혼이 ‘보통 부정적 인 사건’이라고 했으므로 ‘이혼이 대개 가족 관계를 개선한다’는 일반화도 본문과 어긋난다(가능성 → 일반 사실로 바꾼 과잉 일반화 + 본문 에 없는 가치 판단). ① 근거 없음(정답) — 이혼은 대개 가족 관계를 개선하므로 두 번째 관점이 첫 번째 관점보다 더 정확하다. ② 근거 ⓫ — 재평가로 인한 반복적인 단기적 감정 변화는 점차 사람의 장기적인 정신 건강에 영향을 줄 수 있다. ③ 근거 ❽ — 재평가가 슬픔과 분노를 반드시 없애는 것은 아니지만, 그 강도를 줄일 수는 있다. ④ 근거 ❺❾ — 고통스러운 경험조차 다른 각도에서 바라보면 긍정적인 감정을 불러일으킬 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 ❸❻ — 똑같은 고통스러운 사건도 사람이 그것을 어떻게 보느냐에 따라 매우 다른 감정으로 이어질 수 있다.
choice.psg: ❶ Reappraisal — changing the way one thinks about emotional situations — might present a particularly effective avenue to regulating emotions because it transforms emotions at their root. ❷ Take, for example, someone who is going through a divorce. ❸ This is often an adverse event, and yet, it can be construed in different ways. ❹ One might view it as an overpowering loss that will mark one’s family for life. ❺ Alternatively, one might see it as something that is painful but that might lead to positive outcomes in the long run, such as improved relationships. ❻ As a result of these different construals, one might feel different emotions. ❼ The first construal may bring intense sadness and anger. ❽ The second construal might also bring sadness and anger but perhaps at lower levels. ❾ Crucially, it might also bring some positive emotions, such as hope, strength, or gratitude. ❿ This example illustrates how reappraisal might powerfully transform short-term emotional responses. ⓫ When repeated over time, these short-term emotional consequences of reappraisal might accumulate to shape people’s psychological health. ⓬ Thereby, reappraisal might be a key to resilience.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: a single act of reappraisal is enough to permanently change a person’s psychological condition
people’s mental state is determined mainly by the events they experienced in childhood
negative feelings that people hold back collect inside the body and eventually make them physically ill
short-term emotional reactions disappear quickly and leave no lasting effect on how people feel
the momentary emotional effects of reappraising situations, when added together over time, gradually form a person’s lasting mental well-being
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 축적되어 사람들의 심리적 건강을 형성할지도 모른다 → 재평가로 생긴 짧은 감정 변화가 반복되며 쌓여 장기적인 정신 건 강을 만든다 해설: 주어는 ‘these short-term emotional consequences of reappraisal’(❿에서 말한, 재평가가 바꾼 단기적 감정 반응)이고, ‘When repeated over time’이 조건이다. 따라서 ‘축적되어 심리적 건강을 형성한다’ = 한 번 한 번의 짧은 감정 변화가 반복되며 쌓여 장기적인 정신 건강(⓬ 회복 탄력성)을 만든 다는 뜻. ‘억누른 감정이 몸에 쌓여 병이 된다’는 accumulate를 감정 억압으로 오독한 함정, ‘단기 반응은 사라져 영향을 남기지 않는다’는 정반대, ‘단 한 번 의 재평가로 영구히 바뀐다’는 ‘반복’ 조건을 지운 범위 왜곡, ‘어린 시절 사건이 결정한다’는 무관한 내용. ① 단 한 번의 재평가로도 사람의 심리 상태를 영구적으로 바꾸기에 충분하다 ② 사람들의 정신 상태는 주로 어린 시절에 겪은 사건들에 의해 결정된다 ③ 사람들이 억누른 부정적 감정이 몸속에 모여 결국 그들을 신체적으로 병들게 한다 ④ 단기적인 감정 반응은 빠르게 사라지고 사람들의 감정에 지속적인 영향을 남기지 않는다 ⑤ 상황을 재평가하여 생기는 순간적인 감정 효과들이 시간이 지나며 합쳐져 점차 사람의 지속적인 정신적 안녕을 형성한다
choice.body: This example illustrates how reappraisal might powerfully transform short-term emotional responses. When repeated over time, these short-term emotional consequences of reappraisal might accumulate to shape people’s psychological health. Thereby, reappraisal might be a key to resilience.
choice.ul: might accumulate to shape people’s psychological health.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) subjective — (B) identical — (C) fixed regardless of
(A) subjective — (B) varied — (C) tailored to
(A) measurable — (B) identical — (C) tailored to
(A) measurable — (B) varied — (C) tailored to
(A) measurable — (B) varied — (C) fixed regardless of
choice.ex: (A) measurable (B) varied (C) tailored to 근거 ❶❷❸❺❼ 해설: (A) ❷❸ 수질은 특정한 기준(지표)을 따르는 것이고, 지침은 물질이 ‘정확히 얼마나’ 있을 수 있는지 알려 준다 = 측정 가능한 기준 / (B) ❹❺ 마시기 ·작물·보일러 등 so many diverse things = 다양한 / (C) ❼ 활용 방식에 따라 각기 다른 허용치 = 각 용도에 맞춰진. ‘주관적인’ 기준은 ‘정확히 얼마나’를 정하는 ❸과 반대이고, ‘똑같은’ 목적은 ❺의 diverse와 반대이며, ‘용도와 상관없이 고정된’은 ❺❼과 정반대. 요약문 해석: 물을 ‘깨끗하다’고 부르는 것은 그것이 단지 깨끗해 보인다는 것이 아니라 (A) 측정 가능한 기준을 충족한다고 말하는 것이다. 물은 아주 (B) 다양한 목적에 쓰이기 때문에, 물속에 허용되는 불순물의 양은 각 용도에 (C) 맞춰진다.
choice.psg: ❶ When we say that water is “clean,” we don’t just mean that it looks like a glass of water. ❷ Water quality is about following a certain set of criteria, or “benchmarks.” ❸ These guidelines inform us exactly how much physical, chemical, or biological stuff can be in the water. ❹ These rules ensure the water is safe for anything we want to do with it, whether that’s drinking it at home, watering crops on a farm, or running it through a huge industrial boiler. ❺ We can’t utilize the same “one size fits all” rule for everyone because we use water for so many diverse things. ❻ For instance, the water that cools down a huge power plant generator doesn’t need to be as clean as the water you drink from the kitchen tap. ❼ This is why groups set different “safety limits” for the water dependent on how it will be utilized.
choice.body: To call water “clean” is to say that it meets (A)________ standards, not merely that it looks pure. Because water serves such (B)________ purposes, the amount of impurities allowed in it is (C)________ each use.

choice.stem: 다음 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: (A) more — (B) requirements — (C) distinct
(A) less — (B) requirements — (C) distinct
(A) less — (B) requirements — (C) uniform
(A) less — (B) history — (C) distinct
(A) more — (B) history — (C) uniform
choice.ex: (A) less (B) requirements (C) distinct 근거 ❺❻❼ 해설: (A) ❻ doesn’t need to be as clean as the water you drink = 덜 깨끗해도 된다 / (B) ❺❻ 용도마다 필요한 깨끗함의 정도가 다르다 = 그 나름 의 요구 조건 / (C) ❺ ‘one size fits all’ 규칙을 쓸 수 없어 ❼ 각기 다른 허용치 = 별개의 규칙. ‘더 깨끗해야’는 ❻과 반대, ‘역사’는 본문에 없는 근거, ‘획일 적인’ 규칙은 ❺와 정반대. 요약문 해석: 발전소 발전기를 식히는 물은 주방 수도꼭지의 물보다 (A) 덜 깨끗해도 된다. 각 용도에는 그 나름의 (B) 요구 조건이 있으므로, 집단들은 모 두를 위한 하나의 규칙 대신 용도마다 (C) 별개의 규칙을 채택한다.
choice.psg: ❶ When we say that water is “clean,” we don’t just mean that it looks like a glass of water. ❷ Water quality is about following a certain set of criteria, or “benchmarks.” ❸ These guidelines inform us exactly how much physical, chemical, or biological stuff can be in the water. ❹ These rules ensure the water is safe for anything we want to do with it, whether that’s drinking it at home, watering crops on a farm, or running it through a huge industrial boiler. ❺ We can’t utilize the same “one size fits all” rule for everyone because we use water for so many diverse things. ❻ For instance, the water that cools down a huge power plant generator doesn’t need to be as clean as the water you drink from the kitchen tap. ❼ This is why groups set different “safety limits” for the water dependent on how it will be utilized.
choice.body: Water that cools a power plant generator can be (A)________ pure than water from a kitchen tap. Because each use has its own (B)________, groups adopt (C)________ rules for different uses instead of one rule for everyone.

choice.stem: 위 글의 내용으로부터 추론할 수 없는 것을 고르시오.
opt: Groups use different standards for different uses mainly to save money on water treatment.
The wide range of ways people use water makes a single rule for all users impractical.
A glass of water that looks clear may still fail to meet water-quality standards.
Water considered acceptable for one purpose might be unacceptable for another.
Drinking water is generally held to a higher standard than water used to cool machines.
choice.ex: 본문이 밝힌 ‘각기 다른 허용치’의 이유는 ❺ 물을 아주 다양한 일에 쓰기 때문(❻ 용도마다 필요한 깨끗함이 다름)이다. 수처리 비용 절 감이 주된 이유라는 말은 본문에 전혀 없다(그럴듯한 상식으로 원인을 바꾼 거짓 인과). ① 근거 없음(정답) — 집단들은 주로 수처리 비용을 아끼기 위해 용도마다 다른 기준을 사용한다. ② 근거 ❺ — 사람들이 물을 사용하는 방식이 매우 다양해서 모든 사용자를 위한 단일 규칙은 비현실적이다. ③ 근거 ❶❷ — 맑아 보이는 물 한 잔도 여전히 수질 기준을 충족하지 못할 수 있다. ④ 근거 ❻❼ — 한 가지 목적에 적합하다고 여겨지는 물이 다른 목적에는 부적합할 수 있다. ⑤ 근거 ❻ — 마시는 물은 일반적으로 기계를 식히는 데 쓰이는 물보다 더 높은 기준을 적용받는다.
choice.psg: ❶ When we say that water is “clean,” we don’t just mean that it looks like a glass of water. ❷ Water quality is about following a certain set of criteria, or “benchmarks.” ❸ These guidelines inform us exactly how much physical, chemical, or biological stuff can be in the water. ❹ These rules ensure the water is safe for anything we want to do with it, whether that’s drinking it at home, watering crops on a farm, or running it through a huge industrial boiler. ❺ We can’t utilize the same “one size fits all” rule for everyone because we use water for so many diverse things. ❻ For instance, the water that cools down a huge power plant generator doesn’t need to be as clean as the water you drink from the kitchen tap. ❼ This is why groups set different “safety limits” for the water dependent on how it will be utilized.

choice.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것을 고르시오.
opt: separate standards designed for each particular use of water
a rule that every person must use the same amount of water each day
a single water-quality standard applied in the same way to every use of water
a strict standard that applies only to drinking water at home
a rule requiring every water container to be made in the same size
choice.ex: 밑줄 해석: 동일한 ‘일률적인(한 치수로 모두에게 맞추는)’ 규칙 → 용도와 상관없이 모든 물에 똑같이 적용되는 하나의 기준 해설: ‘one size fits all(한 치수로 모두에게 맞춘다)’은 옷 치수에서 온 비유로, 서로 다른 경우를 하나의 기준으로 일괄 처리한다는 뜻. 같은 문장의 ‘because we use water for so many diverse things’와 ❻(발전기 냉각수 vs 수돗물), ❼(용도별 다른 허용치)로 보아 ‘모든 용도에 똑같이 적용되는 하나의 수질 기준’을 가리킨다. ‘용기를 같은 크기로’는 size를 문자 그대로 읽은 함정, ‘용도별 별개 기준’은 필자가 지지하는 정반대 개념, ‘가정 식수에만 적용되는 엄격한 기준’은 범위를 바꾼 왜곡, ‘매일 같은 양의 물 사용’은 무관한 내용. ① 물의 각 특정 용도에 맞게 설계된 별개의 기준들 ② 모든 사람이 매일 같은 양의 물을 써야 한다는 규칙 ③ 물의 모든 용도에 똑같은 방식으로 적용되는 하나의 수질 기준 ④ 가정의 식수에만 적용되는 엄격한 기준 ⑤ 모든 물 용기를 같은 크기로 만들도록 요구하는 규칙
choice.body: These rules ensure the water is safe for anything we want to do with it, whether that’s drinking it at home, watering crops on a farm, or running it through a huge industrial boiler. We can’t utilize the same “one size fits all” rule for everyone because we use water for so many diverse things. For instance, the water that cools down a huge power plant generator doesn’t need to be as clean as the water you drink from the kitchen tap.
choice.ul: the same “one size fits all” rule

order.ex: (단락 구성 ❶❷❸ / ❹❺ / ❻ / ❼❽❾) · ❹ ‘That is no longer the case’의 That은 ❸의 ‘기관들이 분리되어 보호되던 상황’을 가리킴 → ❸ 바로 뒤. ❺ 디지털화의 급증이 ‘더 이상 그렇지 않은’ 이유 · ❻ 자율적으로 소통하는 스마트 시스템 → 그 결과 생긴 연결이 ❼ ‘This interdependence’의 지시 대상 · ❽ ‘As Rita puts it’은 ❸에서 Rita McGrath가 소개된 뒤에만 가능 → ❾ 정보 기술의 새로운 취약성으로 결론
order.A: That is no longer the case. The digitization of massive amounts of information has continued to grow enormously as the cost of computing power has decreased.
order.B: Social media has altered business, politics, and friendships, making going viral a household term. The global financial industry links every bank and countless households in every country, making us vulnerable to human error taking place on the other side of the world. As Columbia University strategy professor Rita McGrath explains, years ago most of our institutions were separate and thereby buffered from the effects of errors outside their walls.
order.C: This interdependence is a breeding ground for complex failure. As Rita puts it, when “things that used to be kept separate bump up against each other, it becomes far more difficult to predict what’s going to happen next.” Information technology creates new vulnerabilities because interconnectedness instantly spreads the impact of small failures.
order.D: The development of smart systems that communicate autonomously gave rise to an infinite variety of potential breakdowns.

order.ex: (단락 구성 ❶ / ❷❸ / ❹❺❻ / ❼❽❾) · ❶ 소셜 미디어 → ❷ 금융 산업: 오늘날 모든 것이 연결된 사례 두 개 → ❸ ‘years ago’ 과거의 분리 상태와 대조 · ❹ That(= ❸의 분리·보호 상태) → ❺❻ 디지털화와 스마트 시스템이 그것을 무너뜨림 · ❼ ‘This interdependence’는 ❻의 자율 소통 시스템을 받으며, ❽ ‘As Rita’는 ❸의 인물 소개 뒤에 와야 함 → ❾ 결론

order.B: The global financial industry links every bank and countless households in every country, making us vulnerable to human error taking place on the other side of the world. As Columbia University strategy professor Rita McGrath explains, years ago most of our institutions were separate and thereby buffered from the effects of errors outside their walls.
order.C: Social media has altered business, politics, and friendships, making going viral a household term.
order.D: This interdependence is a breeding ground for complex failure. As Rita puts it, when “things that used to be kept separate bump up against each other, it becomes far more difficult to predict what’s going to happen next.” Information technology creates new vulnerabilities because interconnectedness instantly spreads the impact of small failures.

order.ex: (단락 구성 ❶ / ❷❸ / ❹ / ❺) · ❶ 주제문(치료와 예방의 진보)이 첫 단락 → ❷❸ 치료의 사례(페니실린) 다음 예방의 출발점(Jenner) — ❶이 treatment → prevention 순으로 제시 · ❹ ‘even led to the elimination of poxvirus’는 천연두(smallpox)가 먼저 소개돼야 성립 → Jenner 문장(❸)으로 끝나는 단락 바로 뒤 · ❺ ‘For other infectious diseases’와 ‘their burden’은 ❹의 백신이 부담을 줄인 질병들과 대비되는 ‘다른’ 질병 → 마지막
order.A: The discovery of penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming, for which he later received the Nobel Prize, was one of the biggest breakthroughs in the battle against infectious diseases. Edward Jenner discovered around 1796 that humans were protected against the deadly smallpox virus after exposure to the cowpox virus, which is harmless to humans.
order.B: Vaccines developed in laboratories have contributed enormously to the reduction of the burden of bacterial and viral diseases and have even led to the elimination of poxvirus.
order.C: Scientific developments and technologies in medical practice have brought us enormous progress in the treatment and prevention of infectious diseases.
order.D: For other infectious diseases (for example cholera and malaria), control and hygiene management measures have reduced their burden, while for others treatment therapies turned viral diseases that were deadly into chronic manageable diseases.

order.C: The discovery of penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming, for which he later received the Nobel Prize, was one of the biggest breakthroughs in the battle against infectious diseases. Edward Jenner discovered around 1796 that humans were protected against the deadly smallpox virus after exposure to the cowpox virus, which is harmless to humans.
order.D: For other infectious diseases (for example cholera and malaria), control and hygiene management measures have reduced their burden, while for others treatment therapies turned viral diseases that were deadly into chronic manageable diseases.

order.ex: (단락 구성 ❶ / ❷❸❹ / ❺❻ / ❼❽) · ❷ ‘We’re much too close’는 ❶ ‘we are not the user’의 이유(우리는 만든 것에 너무 가까워 객관적으로 볼 수 없음) · ❹ ‘So how can designers …?’ 질문 → ❺ ‘An incredibly effective way is …’가 그 답(사용성 테스트) · ❻ ‘The goal of this method’ → ❼ ‘This technique’, ❽ ‘this method’는 모두 ❺의 usability testing을 받음
order.A: This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.
order.B: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user.
order.C: We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective?
order.D: An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities.

Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.

read.ko: 실험실에서 개발된 백신은 세균성 질병과 바이러스성 질병의 부담을 줄이는 데 엄청나게 기여했으며, 심지어 폭스바이러스(천연두 바이러스)의 퇴치로까 지 이어졌다.
read.en: Vaccines developed in laboratories have contributed enormously to the reduction of the burden of bacterial and viral diseases and have even led to the elimination of poxvirus.

read.ko: 예를 들어 콜레라와 말라리아 같은 다른 전염병의 경우에는 통제와 위생 관리 조치들이 그것들의 부담을 줄였으며, 또 다른 것들의 경우에는 치료법이 치 명적인 바이러스성 질병을 만성적이고 관리 가능한 질병으로 바꾸었다.
read.en: For other infectious diseases (for example cholera and malaria), control and hygiene management measures have reduced their burden, while for others treatment therapies turned viral diseases that were deadly into chronic manageable diseases.

read.ko: 디자이너들이 더 효과적인 제품과 경험을 만들어 내기 위해 수용해야만 하는 단순한 진리는 우리가 ‘사용자가 아니라’는 사실이다.
read.en: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user.

read.ko: 우리는 우리가 만드는 것에 너무 가까워서 그것을 객관적으로 보고 사용자들이 그것과 어떻게 상호 작용할지 이해할 수 없다.
read.en: We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it.

read.ko: 가장 좋은 사용자 인터페이스들은 실제 사용자들과 그들의 그것들과의 상호 작용에 대한 관찰 결과들에 의해 만들어져 온 것들이다.
read.en: The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them.

read.ko: 그러면 디자이너들은 어떻게 자신의 작업이 더 효과적일 수 있도록 만들 수 있을까?
read.en: So how can designers shape their work to be more effective?

read.ko: 한 가지 엄청나게 효과적인 방법은 사용성 테스트를 가지고 하는 것이다.
read.en: An incredibly effective way is with usability testing.

read.ko: 이 방법의 목표는 참가자들이 실제적인 활동들에 참여하도록 요청함으로써 디자인상의 문제들을 밝혀 내고, 현재 있는 가능성들을 발견하고, 사용자들의 행동들과 선호하는 것들에 대해 더 많이 학습하는 것이다.
read.en: The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities.

read.ko: 이 기술은 디자인이 실제 사용자들의 손 안에 있을 때 그것이 얼마나 잘 작동할 것인지를 이해하는 데 효과적이다.
read.en: This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users.

read.ko: 디자이너들은 대표적인 사용자들로부터 발견한 것들에 기반한 차후의 수정들을 통해 그들의 작업물을 개선하기 위해 이 방법을 사용할 수 있다.
read.en: Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.

read.en: Reappraisal — changing the way one thinks about emotional situations — might present a particularly effective avenue to regulating emotions because it transforms emotions at their root.

read.ko: 예를 들어, 이혼을 겪고 있는 누군가를 생각해 보자.
read.en: Take, for example, someone who is going through a divorce.

read.ko: 이것은 보통 부정적인 사건이지만, 그럼에도 불구하고 그것은 다른 방식들로 해석될 수 있다.
read.en: This is often an adverse event, and yet, it can be construed in different ways.

read.ko: 누군가는 그것을 자신의 가족에게 평생 흔적을 남길 강렬한 상실로 여길지도 모른다.
read.en: One might view it as an overpowering loss that will mark one’s family for life.

read.ko: 이와는 달리, 누군가는 그것을 고통스럽기는 하지만 개선된 관계와 같이 장기적으로는 긍정적인 결과로 이어질 수 있는 일로 여길지도 모른다.
read.en: Alternatively, one might see it as something that is painful but that might lead to positive outcomes in the long run, such as improved relationships.

read.ko: 이러한 다른 해석들의 결과로서 누군가는 다른 감정들을 느낄지도 모른다.
read.en: As a result of these different construals, one might feel different emotions.

read.ko: 첫 번째 해석은 강렬한 슬픔과 분노를 불러올 수 있다.
read.en: The first construal may bring intense sadness and anger.

read.ko: 두 번째 해석 역시 슬픔과 분노를 불러올지도 모르지만, 아마도 더 낮은 강도로 그러할지도 모른다.
read.en: The second construal might also bring sadness and anger but perhaps at lower levels.

read.ko: 결정적으로 그것은 희망, 강인함 또는 감사함과 같은 어떤 긍정적인 감정들 또한 불러올지도 모른다.
read.en: Crucially, it might also bring some positive emotions, such as hope, strength, or gratitude.

read.ko: 이 예시는 재평가가 어떻게 단기적인 감정적 반응들을 강력하게 변화시킬 수 있을지를 보여 준다.
read.en: This example illustrates how reappraisal might powerfully transform short-term emotional responses.

read.ko: 오랫동안 반복되면, 재평가의 이러한 단기적인 감정적 결과들이 축적되어 사람들의 심리적 건강을 형성할지도 모른다.
read.en: When repeated over time, these short-term emotional consequences of reappraisal might accumulate to shape people’s psychological health.

read.ko: 그렇게 함으로써 재평가는 회복 탄력성의 해답이 될지도 모른다.
read.en: Thereby, reappraisal might be a key to resilience.

read.ko: 우리가 물이 ‘깨끗하다’라고 말할 때, 우리는 단지 그것이 마실 물 한 잔처럼 보인다는 것을 의미하지는 않는다.
read.en: When we say that water is “clean,” we don’t just mean that it looks like a glass of water.

read.ko: 수질은 특정한 기준들의 집합, 즉 ‘지표들’을 따르는 것에 관한 것이다.
read.en: Water quality is about following a certain set of criteria, or “benchmarks.”

read.ko: 이러한 지침들은 우리에게 정확히 얼마나 많은 물리적, 화학적, 혹은 생물학적인 것들이 물 안에 있을 수 있는지를 알려 준다.
read.en: These guidelines inform us exactly how much physical, chemical, or biological stuff can be in the water.

read.ko: 이러한 규칙들은 집에서 마시든, 농장에서 작물에 물을 주든, 거대한 산업용 보일러에 흘려보내든, 우리가 물로 하고 싶은 어떤 일에도 그 물이 안전하도록 보장한다.
read.en: These rules ensure the water is safe for anything we want to do with it, whether that’s drinking it at home, watering crops on a farm, or running it through a huge industrial boiler.

read.ko: 우리가 물을 아주 많은 다양한 일에 사용하기 때문에 우리는 동일한 ‘일률적인’ 규칙을 모두에게 활용할 수 없다.
read.en: We can’t utilize the same “one size fits all” rule for everyone because we use water for so many diverse things.

read.ko: 예를 들어, 거대한 발전소의 발전기를 식히는 물은 여러분이 주방 수도꼭지로부터 마시는 물만큼 깨끗할 필요가 없다.
read.en: For instance, the water that cools down a huge power plant generator doesn’t need to be as clean as the water you drink from the kitchen tap.

read.ko: 이것이 물이 어떻게 활용될지에 따라 집단들이 그것에 대한 각기 다른 ‘안전 허용치’를 설정하는 이유이다.
read.en: This is why groups set different “safety limits” for the water dependent on how it will be utilized.

para.en: Social media has altered business, politics, and friendships, making going viral a household term. The global financial industry links every bank and countless households in every country, making us vulnerable to human error taking place on the other side of the world. As Columbia University strategy professor Rita McGrath explains, years ago most of our institutions were separate and thereby buffered from the effects of errors outside their walls. That is no longer the case. The digitization of massive amounts of information has continued to grow enormously as the cost of computing power has decreased. The development of smart systems that communicate autonomously gave rise to an infinite variety of potential breakdowns. This interdependence is a breeding ground for complex failure. As Rita puts it, when “things that used to be kept separate bump up against each other, it becomes far more difficult to predict what’s going to happen next.” Information technology creates new vulnerabilities because interconnectedness instantly spreads the impact of small failures.

Scientific developments and technologies in medical practice have brought us enormous progress in the treatment and prevention of infectious diseases. The discovery of penicillin in 1928 by Alexander Fleming, for which he later received the Nobel Prize, was one of the biggest breakthroughs in the battle against infectious diseases. Edward Jenner discovered around 1796 that humans were protected against the deadly smallpox virus after exposure to the cowpox virus, which is harmless to humans. Vaccines developed in laboratories have contributed enormously to the reduction of the burden of bacterial and viral diseases and have even led to the elimination of poxvirus. For other infectious diseases (for example cholera and malaria), control and hygiene management measures have reduced their burden, while for others treatment therapies turned viral diseases that were deadly into chronic manageable diseases.

A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.

Reappraisal — changing the way one thinks about emotional situations — might present a particularly effective avenue to regulating emotions because it transforms emotions at their root. Take, for example, someone who is going through a divorce. This is often an adverse event, and yet, it can be construed in different ways. One might view it as an overpowering loss that will mark one’s family for life. Alternatively, one might see it as something that is painful but that might lead to positive outcomes in the long run, such as improved relationships. As a result of these different construals, one might feel different emotions. The first construal may bring intense sadness and anger. The second construal might also bring sadness and anger but perhaps at lower levels. Crucially, it might also bring some positive emotions, such as hope, strength, or gratitude. This example illustrates how reappraisal might powerfully transform short-term emotional responses. When repeated over time, these short-term emotional consequences of reappraisal might accumulate to shape people’s psychological health. Thereby, reappraisal might be a key to resilience.

When we say that water is “clean,” we don’t just mean that it looks like a glass of water. Water quality is about following a certain set of criteria, or “benchmarks.” These guidelines inform us exactly how much physical, chemical, or biological stuff can be in the water. These rules ensure the water is safe for anything we want to do with it, whether that’s drinking it at home, watering crops on a farm, or running it through a huge industrial boiler. We can’t utilize the same “one size fits all” rule for everyone because we use water for so many diverse things. For instance, the water that cools down a huge power plant generator doesn’t need to be as clean as the water you drink from the kitchen tap. This is why groups set different “safety limits” for the water dependent on how it will be utilized.
